title: Set-Asides on the Standing of the Protection Cover Behind an Account
content:
A part of the qualifying monthly earnings of a Keyturn Host Payout Account is set aside where a claim has lately been appraised under the protection cover behind the account, and more of it where that cover is not in good standing. The cover in question is the host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment.

1. **Where the protection enrolment behind the account stands in good order and a claim has been appraised under it in the twelve months up to that day**, the claim reduction share of 10 percent is set aside.
2. **Where the protection enrolment behind the account is suspended and a claim has been appraised under it in that period**, the suspended reduction share of 25 percent is set aside.
3. **In every other case**, nothing is set aside on that ground, the share standing at 0 percent.

The share is taken on the qualifying monthly earnings as first measured, and the sum set aside is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## The two tests

Both of the first two cases require a claim appraised under the enrolment in the twelve months up to that day. Where no claim has been appraised in that period, neither of them can be met and the third governs however the cover stands. Where a claim has been appraised in that period, the standing of the enrolment decides between the first two: good order gives 10 percent, and suspension gives 25 percent.

## On hypothetical figures

Where the qualifying monthly earnings as first measured are 1200.00 USD, the sum set aside on this ground is 120.00 USD in the first case, 300.00 USD in the second and nothing at all in the third.

The records that settle both tests are the host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment, which carries the ground on which it stands suspended where it is suspended, and the claim records under it, which carry the day each claim was appraised.
